name: 3039-batchdecode-llama31-8b-8gpu
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the ungated mirror of meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (same weights, same config, ~15 GB, bf16); the Llama 3.1 Community License applies.
hardware: 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one node, no router and no external cache tier.
parallelism: TP=8, PP=1, DP=1, EP=1. An 8B model fits on one card; eight is the declared setup, not a fit requirement.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=64, warmup the first 20%, bounded at 6400 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text` over /v1/completions, single turn, no prefix buckets, seed 42: prompts exactly 32 tokens (stdev 0), generations pinned at exactly 512 tokens with `ignore_eos: true` and `temperature: 0.0`.
purpose: A long-form text generation service on an 8B model, serving 64 concurrent users short prompts across eight GPUs.
launch:
# Flat `key: value` only -- an indented or nested line is skipped by the engine's parser and it
# then starts without what this file declares. host/port/served-model-name are set outside it.
model-path: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
tp-size: 8

# Exactly what this engine resolves to on an H100 when the key is absent, so it changes no
# behaviour; written out so a venv lacking the wheel fails loudly at startup instead of quietly
# serving a different machine.
attention-backend: flashinfer

# A ceiling on the running batch. It sizes ReqToTokenPool at 129 slots, which caps the scheduler
# at 128 admitted requests, so the running batch stays inside the captured CUDA-graph sizes
# however far client concurrency is walked; above the cap the server queues. Removing it silently
# changes the machine.
max-running-requests: 128
